findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical rightmost-non-nine carry solution. It scans once to identify the only digit that may increment, zeroes precisely the forced suffix, and allocates only the required leading node for an all-nine number. Its linked-list state is clear and conventional, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 369 and its Python plusOne surface. The Reference preserves most-significant-digit-first representation, nonnegative integer semantics, carry-created leading digits, both source examples in order, and all three list and digit constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064621041. Its last-non-nine scan, all-nine leading-node branch, zeroing passes, increment, and returned head are identical to the protected app-local algorithm; the explicit local ListNode is the permitted adapter for LeetCode's injected model.

The legal all-nine tiers contain 4, 20, and 100 nodes, span 25x, reach the source node-count maximum, and force carry through the entire list. The current source passes all 11 executions at +0.02 relative growth and 1.01x; correct repeated predecessor search passes every benchmark output but fails only scaling at +0.80 and 13.63x.

The Approach accurately derives the rightmost carry-stopping digit, all-nine length increase, unchanged prefix, O(n) time, and O(1) auxiliary space. Its app-contract paragraph now describes the actual `ListNode(1, head)` construction instead of a different node factory.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples in order, significant-digit orientation, plus-one result semantics, leading-zero rule, and all three constraints.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order with their exact digit lists and outputs; the invented carry examples are correctly labelled trials.
The one-node zero and nine cases cover the minimum list length and both digit bounds, while benchmark and generated checks cover the 100-node maximum without introducing a leading zero.
No carry, one trailing nine, several trailing nines, an internal non-suffix nine, a carry stopping in the middle, and an all-nine length increase cover every decimal carry shape.
An independent decimal-conversion oracle verified all eight authored results, all three benchmark results, all 100,000 legal values through five digits, and 1,000 random 100-node values.
All eight correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged legal 4-, 20-, and 100-node all-nine workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
